name: Operating Cadence and Accountability

positioning.oneLineSummary: Evaluates whether planning, reviews, metrics, decisions, and communication form a repeated learning-and-accountability loop.
positioning.productLabel: Operating Cadence Lens — based on Claire Hughes Johnson's public Scaling People materials

attribution.display: Based on Claire Hughes Johnson's public Scaling People materials

neutralParaphrase: A useful cadence repeatedly connects goals and metrics with business review, decisions, ownership, communication, and follow-through. The exact rhythm is company-specific; its value comes from creating reliable touchpoints, learning from results, and improving the mechanism.

locator.value: Operating to Win transcript p. 2, 00:04:06-07:31: repeatable stability points, reviews, goals, dashboards, metrics, all-hands, and no secret cadence
Q&A: systems and operating cadence across week, month, quarter, planning, and leadership meetings
Young companies section, lines 73-75: important goals and metrics recognized and reviewed publicly
Transcript lines 149-157: operating practices serve outsized results and leaders should track outcomes

requiredConditions: The company has repeated work and cross-person or cross-team coordination.
Goals and outcome measures can be distinguished from activity measures.
The review covers decisions and follow-through, not calendars alone.

requiredEvidence.description: Company, division, and team goals; metric definitions; owners; targets; and connections to long-term goals.
Planning, business review, leadership, team, all-hands, and decision forums with purpose, participants, inputs, outputs, and frequency.
Decisions, owners, deadlines, escalation paths, completed actions, and later review.
Time cost, participant burden, duplicated forums, experiments, review dates, and changes to the cadence.

decisionQuestions: Which decisions and outcomes does each recurring forum serve?
Are goals and metrics understood consistently and reviewed at a useful frequency?
Do reviews produce owners, actions, and later accountability?
Which meetings duplicate work or exist without a decision purpose?
How does the company learn that a cadence should change?
positiveSignals: Metrics have definitions, owners, and links to goals.
Reviews produce recorded decisions and accountable follow-through.
Cadence changes when stage or evidence changes.
Communication repeats important context across appropriate channels without creating conflicting truth.
redFlags: Activity metrics substitute for customer, financial, quality, or delivery outcomes.
The same decision is repeatedly reopened without ownership.
Meetings have no defined input, output, or decision right.
A borrowed cadence persists despite high cost and low use.
disconfirmingEvidence: An informal cadence is effective for a small, tightly coordinated team.
A temporary increase in meeting frequency supports a crisis, launch, or incident.
Low metric frequency is appropriate for a long-cycle business.
A missed goal prompted a documented strategy correction rather than weak accountability.
contraindications: Do not prescribe a universal cadence.
Do not let dashboards substitute for verified metric definitions or decisions.
Do not infer causality from cadence and performance correlation alone.

instructions: Map goals, metric definitions, owners, and review frequencies.
Map each forum to decisions, outputs, and follow-through.
Trace selected goals from planning through review to outcome or correction.
Conclude coherent, emerging, ceremonial, burdensome, or insufficient.

deterministicRule.prohibition: The language model must not invent meeting frequency, metric values, or action completion.

sourceReliability.high: Versioned goals, metric lineage, decisions, actions, outcomes, and participant evidence converge.

evidenceStrength.medium: Cadence repeatedly produces decisions and actions.
evidenceStrength.high: Traceable review-to-action-to-outcome loops operate and adapt.

evidenceCoverage.high: Definitions, owners, forums, decisions, actions, costs, changes, and counterevidence covered.

applicabilityConfidence.high: Execution materially depends on repeated cross-team coordination.

judgmentConfidence.medium: Multiple traceable loops support a bounded judgment.
judgmentConfidence.high: Longitudinal operating and outcome evidence supports the conclusion.

empiricalQualifications: High-performing companies may adopt more process because of complexity.
Cadence effectiveness depends on stage and work cycle.

rights.notes: Public author materials are neutrally paraphrased.

openIssues: Define normalized meeting-load and action-follow-through measures.
